title: Chase Across the Glass Mere
story: Skimmerwick the Pond Shade has swiped the village's thaw-bell and gone skating off across the frozen mere, giggling like cracking ice. Without the bell, spring simply will not start. Mr 6 straps on blades, but the shade already has a head start — so he works out exactly how long the chase will take.
question: Skimmerwick glides in a straight line at 9 leagues per hour and has a 20-minute head start. Mr 6 skates the same line at 13.5 leagues per hour. How many minutes after Mr 6 starts will he catch the shade?
solution: In its 20-minute head start, Skimmerwick covers 9 × (20 ÷ 60) = 3 leagues.
Mr 6 closes the gap at 13.5 - 9 = 4.5 leagues per hour, so he needs 3 ÷ 4.5 = 2/3 of an hour.
praise: Turning the head start into a distance was the key move — the next step is dividing that gap by how fast the gap SHRINKS, not by either skater's full speed.
hint: First turn the 20-minute head start into leagues, then ask how much closer Mr 6 gets each hour.
victory: Exactly forty minutes later Mr 6 skates up beside the shade, holds out a mitten, and asks politely for the bell back. Skimmerwick, astonished that anyone did the arithmetic, hands it over and melts into a sheepish puff of frost.
imagePrompt: A caped numeral-six knight on ice skates racing a translucent grinning shade across a vast moonlit frozen lake, long blue shadows and a stolen bronze bell glinting ahead.
